chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Nu'man, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu al-Nu'man! Do not lie against us with a single lie, lest you be deprived of al-hanifiyyah (true faith/straightness), and do not seek to become a leader (or head) so that you become a tail (or follower), and do not make the people dependent on us (by claiming our authority) so that you become poor, for you will inevitably be stopped and questioned. So if you are truthful, we will confirm you, and if you lie, we will contradict you.'

key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّةَ: True faith or straightness in religion, often associated with the pure monotheism of Ibrahim (as).
key_terms.تَسْتَأْكِلِ: To make dependent or to seek reliance through someone else's authority.
key_terms.ذَنَباً: Tail, implying a follower or one of lesser status, often used in contrast to 'head'.
key_terms.رَأْساً: Head/leader, implying a position of prominence or authority.
key_terms.مَوْقُوفٌ: Stopped/standing for account, referring to the Day of Judgment or a moment of reckoning.

ai.seo_question: What are the consequences of lying about the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'hanifiyyah' (upright monotheistic faith) as a fragile trust that can be lost through a single lie about the Imams, a principle central to Shia epistemology regarding the reliability of narrators. Imam Abu Ja'far (asws) further warns against social climbing and using the Imams' names for material gain, emphasizing the ultimate accountability where the Imams themselves will verify the truthfulness of their followers. This serves as a reminder that spiritual status is contingent upon sincerity and truthfulness in conveying the divine message.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Al Nu’man who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Al-Nu’man! Do not lie against us<sup>asws</sup> (or) your true Religion would be Confiscated, and do not seek to become a leader for it would happen to be a sin, and do not devour (earn from) the people through us<sup>asws</sup>, for you would be poor, for you would be Paused inevitably and Questioned. So if you were truthful we<sup>asws</sup> would ratify you, and if you lie, we<sup>asws</sup> would belie you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu al-Nu’man who has said the following:

“Once abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to me, ‘O abu al-Nu’man, do not forge lies against us; it removes (your) true belief. Do not seek to be the head to become a sin and do not use people as means of your earning through us; it will make you poor. You will be held accountable and will be stopped for interrogations. If you speak the truth we will certify you and, if you lie, we will reject you.’”
